messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: runtime-east nodes reporting sustained KV cache metadata growth + continuous-batching blowups. Auto-throttle kicked but not stabilizing. Paging increasing, block manager frees not keeping up. Paging pressure -> downstream latency spikes. Pushing thread to oncall. @Maria Diaz @Samir Patel please triage.

Maria Diaz: on it. seeing metadata size jump on blockmgr across the fleet, per-node metadata ~1.1GB -> 1.8GB over 6m, evictions not reclaiming. continuous-batcher reported batch_count jumps (50 -> 1200) and avg batch_tokens 6k.

Samir Patel: ack. preliminary cause looks like a regression in batching heuristics that widened batch window under a specific traffic pattern (many short prompts with identical prefixes). That caused tons of duplicated KV entries + larger block allocations.

Alex Kim: customer impact? any 5xx/429s?

Maria Diaz: a handful of customers (~5 orgs) show 95th latency spikes from 200ms -> 2.5s and intermittent 429s from per-route token throttles. No data loss.

Jill Chen: propose immediate mitigations: 1) lower continuous-batcher.max_tokens from 4096 -> 1024 (hot config rollout), 2) set batch_window_ms cap to 50, 3) disable kv-prefetch in runtime-east canary pool, 4) force blockmgr GC pass.

Samir Patel: agree. also change block_manager.target_block_kb from 8192 -> 4096 to limit per-block metadata blowup. tweak eviction_policy to 'size-based-lru' for the canary. We'll make a scoped canary change first.

Maria Diaz: creating canary config patch now. will roll to 3 nodes and monitor.

Jill Chen: kubectl snippets for hotfix (runbook):
```bash
# patch configmap for canary pool
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap blockmgr-config -p '{"data":{"target_block_kb":"4096","eviction_policy":"size-based-lru","continuous_batcher_max_tokens":"1024","continuous_batcher_window_ms":"50"}}'
# trigger rolling restart of canary pods
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart ds/blockmgr-canary
# force metadata GC job
kubectl -n runtime create job --from=cronjob/metadata-gc force-metadata-gc-$(date +%s)
```

Kevin O'Leary: if the canary fails, what's rollback?

Samir Patel: rollback is immediate: revert configmap patch and restart canary pods. Also we have feature-flag to disable new batching heuristics (FF: new_batching_algo=false).

Laura Barnes: I'll prepare a short customer note if the canary shows improvement. Suggested: brief ETA + impact (latency spikes, transient throttles), no data loss, engineers working on hotfix.

Maria Diaz: canary patch applied to 3 nodes at 1747890150. initial metrics: metadata growth rate reduced ~60% within 30s, batch sizes dropping. still seeing two noisy nodes, investigating.

Alex Kim: logs from one noisy node:
```
[2025-06-12T14:42:30Z] block_manager: alloc_block size=5242880 metadata_size=256k entries=12000
[2025-06-12T14:42:31Z] continuous_batcher: batch_open window_ms=3200 tokens=10240
[2025-06-12T14:42:31Z] eviction: failed_to_reclaim candidates=0
```

Samir Patel: weird — eviction candidates=0 suggests metadata bookkeeping corrupted for some blocks. schedule a metadata-scrub job on the two noisy nodes.

Jill Chen: running scrub now on node runtime-east-03. command: `/opt/bin/blockmgr-scrub --dry-run` then actual run after validating.

Maria Diaz: scrub dry-run shows ~18k stale metadata entries on the node. will run actual scrub at 1747890188.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: METADATA SCRUB STARTED on runtime-east-03 by Jill Chen.

Laura Barnes: customer comm draft: "We're investigating a runtime cache issue causing increased latency for a subset of requests in East region. We're rolling a targeted config patch now; no data loss. We'll update in 30m or when improved." any additions?

Kevin O'Leary: include actions taken and rollback plan. also ask impacted customers if they can route to other regions temporarily.

Maria Diaz: scrub completed at 1747890198, reclaimed ~22MB metadata and reduced stale entries to ~200. node metrics show eviction candidates now present, evictions running.

Samir Patel: canary looks good at +15s post-scrub: batch counts back to normal, metadata growth flat. rolling to next 10 nodes.

Laura Barnes: sending customer note now.

Incident Bot: Monitor: dashboards/runtime/kv-metadata and dashboards/runtime/batch-sizes. Oncall handoff: @Samir Patel -> oncall shift until 1747893800. If regressions reappear escalate to eng-runtime.

Maria Diaz: updating runbook with the scrub steps and the config caps. closing the immediate surge, leaving follow-up tasks: deeper postmortem to find why eviction candidates were zero and whether the new batching heuristic missed dedup opportunities.

Samir Patel: noted. follow-ups: 1) reproduce locally with truncated traffic pattern, 2) add guard in batching to dedupe identical prefixes, 3) add additional telemetry for block-level metadata accounting.

Kevin O'Leary: :thumbsup: good job team.

Incident Bot: THREAD CLOSED for immediate mitigation. follow-up tasks filed in ENG-INC-3123.
